title: Maximum Gap Between Stations
summary: Given two strings, skill and station, each of length n and m respectively, assign each worker to a unique station such that skill[i] matches station[j] for all i, and the station indices assigned to the workers must be strictly increasing.
statement: Given two strings, skill and station, each of length n and m respectively, assign each worker to a unique station such that skill[i] matches station[j] for all i, and the station indices assigned to the workers must be strictly increasing. The maximum gap is defined as the largest difference between the station indices assigned to two consecutive workers in any valid assignment. If there is only one worker, the gap is 0.
constraints: Assign each skill character to an equal station character at strictly increasing indices.
skill is guaranteed to be a subsequence of station.
Maximize the largest gap between consecutive assigned indices; return zero for one worker.
hints: For each skill position, compute its latest feasible station index by scanning backward.
Scan forward to obtain each current worker’s earliest feasible index.
Pair the earliest position for i with the latest feasible position for i+1.
Any optimal consecutive gap can move its left endpoint earlier and right endpoint later without invalidating surrounding assignments.
editorial: Any optimal consecutive gap can move its left endpoint earlier and right endpoint later without invalidating surrounding assignments.
